meta.formacaoDescricao: Three steps, eleven notebooks: the training of the Lúcia Maria Revolutionary School.

formacao.lead: Three steps, eleven notebooks. Each notebook has **side A**, theory, **side B**, practice, a task in the world and a circle in the nucleus. The lesson count is the real one: what has not been written yet shows as "in preparation".

degraus.desc: Which side you are on, and the first step to get organized.
Talking, organizing the neighborhood and the workplace, communicating and taking care.
Analyzing the political moment, training newcomers and keeping memory.

como.titulo: How to move up a step
como.estudarTexto: Do the ready lessons of the step's notebooks. No grades: feedback is by competence.
como.praticarTexto: Carry out the tasks in the world and tell the nucleus how it went.
como.bancaTexto: A circle with the nucleus and the person who accompanies you: review, criticism and self-criticism, and the next step opens.

lista: For a week, write down what your work and your neighborhood have to do with what you studied: prices, wages, rent, transport. Bring it to the nucleus, without names.
Go to a meeting of an organization near you (association, union, collective) and note how it works. Then tell the nucleus.
Start a difficult conversation with someone in your family or at work. Listen more than you speak. Then tell the nucleus what you learned.
Walk around your neighborhood and draw a simple map of the problems and of the places where people meet. Bring the map to the nucleus, without names or home addresses.
Talk one-on-one with a coworker about a common problem at work. Write down what you heard, without the name, and bring it to the nucleus.
Write a short news story about something in your neighborhood, check every piece of information before publishing and bring it to the nucleus to read together.
Review with someone from the nucleus the security of your phone and your message groups. Agree on a collective care and tell how it went.
Write a one-page summary of the month's political situation, with sources, and present it in the nucleus circle.
Prepare and lead a short study circle with the nucleus or with newcomers. Then review it together.
With permission, record a memory conversation with an older person from the struggle or the neighborhood, and keep it the way the notebook teaches.
During the year, take part in an organization in your neighborhood, workplace or school, and write down, without names, what you learned from it.
